reference: No GNU CLI implements this Bash builtin's verb interface. Contract expectations use the exported http_doc usage text, HTTP/1.1 message framing (RFC 9112), and hand-constructed URL/request/response fixtures. The request golden bytes are independently assembled from the stated method, origin-form target, headers, and UTF-8 body byte length; no candidate output is used as an oracle. Bash type/help builtins provide the metadata contract.
coverage: URL parsing with IPv6, explicit port, query without slash, fragment removal, and -V binding
Exact POST request framing, caller header, UTF-8 body byte length, CRLF separators, and no appended newline
Rejection of method and header line injection with no partial stdout
Response-body extraction of a binary body containing NUL and status binding
Successful empty 204 response and truncation of an existing output file
Malformed status rejection without replacing an existing output file
exclusions: No matching GNU http CLI exists, so no case is mislabeled as GNU parity.
No network, TLS, DNS, redirect, chunked-transfer, or connection-reuse operation is run; end-to-end loopback coverage is deferred.
The fixtures do not exercise response header-size limits, request aggregate-header limits, stdout write failures, or readonly-variable failure paths.

cases.purpose: Bash type/help metadata must expose http as a builtin and provide its documented verb synopsis.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t http) == builtin ]] || exit 1
help http > help.out
doc=$(<help.out)
[[ $doc == *"HTTP/1.1 URL and request framing helpers."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *"response-body RESPONSE_FILE"* ]] || exit 1
printf 'builtin-and-help-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Parse a bracketed IPv6 URL with explicit port, a query without an explicit slash, and a local fragment; bind the documented result with -V.
Compare emitted bytes with an independently hand-encoded HTTP/1.1 POST: origin-form target, generated headers, custom header, UTF-8 Content-Length, CRLF framing, and no extra trailing newline.
cases.stdout:
POST /path?q=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test:8080
User-Agent: bash-os/0.1
Accept: */*
X-Fixture: yes
Content-Length: 5
Connection: close

café

cases.purpose: Reject a method containing a line break and a caller header containing an injected second line, returning usage failure without emitting a partial request.
cases.script:
attempt=0
reject() {
  attempt=$((attempt+1))
  if "$@" > "captured-$attempt.out" 2> "captured-$attempt.err"; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
  [[ $rc == 2 && ! -s captured-$attempt.out && -s captured-$attempt.err ]]
}
reject http request 'http://example.test/' -X $'GET\nInjected: yes'
reject http request 'http://example.test/' -H $'X-Fixture: yes\r\nInjected: yes'
printf 'injection-rejected\n'

cases.purpose: Extract a deterministic body containing an embedded NUL, bind its 200 status, and verify the output bytes using Bash read builtins.
cases.script:
printf 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 3\r\n\r\na\0b' > response.in
http response-body response.in -o body.out -S status
[[ $status == 200 ]]
printf '%s\n' "$status"
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; import sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(Path("body.out").read_bytes())'

cases.purpose: Accept a valid empty 204 response body, bind its status, and leave the output file empty even when it previously contained data.
cases.script:
printf 'HTTP/1.1 204 No Content\r\n\r\n' > response.in
printf stale > body.out
http response-body response.in -o body.out -S status
[[ $status == 204 && ! -s body.out ]] || exit 1
printf 'status=204 empty-body\n'

cases.purpose: Reject a malformed HTTP status line and preserve an existing destination file rather than replacing it with an untrusted body.
cases.script:
printf 'HTTP/1.1 200oops\r\n\r\nreplacement' > response.in
printf original > body.out
if http response-body response.in -o body.out; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc == 1 && $(<body.out) == original ]] || exit 1
printf 'malformed-response-rejected-preserved\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise an end-to-end request and response transaction through the surrounding socket/TLS integration.
Frame an empty GET request into a shell variable with the documented default target and no appended newline.
cases.stdout:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.test
User-Agent: bash-os/0.1
Accept: */*
Content-Length: 0
Connection: close

cases.purpose: Extract an independently supplied HTTP 404 body and bind the status while returning failure.
cases.script:
printf 'HTTP/1.0 404 Missing
Content-Length: 4

lost' > response.in; if http response-body response.in -o body.out -S status; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi; printf '%s:%s:%s
' "$rc" "$status" "$(<body.out)"
